title: Grateful Dead Live at Colden Auditorium, Queens College on 1970-10-10

ai_review.summary: Muddy but listenable audience tape of a classic 1970 show that shines on the The Other One → NFA jam and an electric Deep Elem Blues.
ai_review.review: The performance is solid – fans repeatedly point out the monster The Other One into Nothing Fixed About sequence, a rare electric Deep Elem Blues, and deep‑time jams that capture the ’70 Dead vibe.  The audience recording is typical of early‑70 AUDs: hissy, a bit muddy and sometimes distant (recorded from a projection booth), with a few missing tracks, but it still conveys the concert’s energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical content (especially The Other One → NFA) while noting consistent audio shortcomings; weighted blend of strong show quality and fair recording yields a ~4.2 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical AUD hiss and muddiness, distant sound from a projection‑booth mic, occasional drop‑outs, and several missing songs (e.g., Viola Lee Blues, later set).

standout_songs: The Other One → Nothing Fixed About
show_quality.setlist_flow: One‑set show typical of early 1970 concerts; strong mid‑set jam flow with The Other One/NFA as the high point, but the recording cuts off several closing numbers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His tentative vocal on Deep Elem and a repetitive three‑note phrase on Viola Lee Blues are noted; otherwise his guitar work during the jams is praised.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum segment leading into NFA is highlighted (some call it ‘Crptical>Drums>TOO>NFA!’) but described as nothing special.
